metadata.title: styxx v7.48.1 — security repair: a capsule or an audited certificate chose where styxx wrote files, and now every name it gives must be a bare file name
metadata.description:
This version continues the styxx software record (v6.2.0, the reference implementation of the Cognometric Fingerprint Specification v1.0, 10.5281/zenodo.19746215; its deposited foundations outline predates the 2026-06-21 scope note, D5 in zenodo/MANIFEST.json) and belongs to the Fathom research series (10.5281/zenodo.19326174).

styxx v7.48.1, released 2026-10-06: a security patch release. This record holds the Python package exactly as published on PyPI and the source tree at the git tag v7.48.1 (commit b42942186015848daa32e40b95970f4e370a3016). It is a version in the styxx software concept record 10.5281/zenodo.19758618, which resolves to the latest version. styxx 7.48.0, the release this one patches, is 10.5281/zenodo.23042251 in the same concept (released 2026-09-25).

The release carries one security repair, the version bump that conformance/sworn/ moves with, and what merged on main after 7.48.0. The next two sections, the security repair and what else the release carries, are condensed from the ## [7.48.1] section of CHANGELOG.md in this tree, where the full entries are. Every number in them is as that section prints it, and each line keeps the limits its source states. The list of stale or wrong lines after them comes from that section's errata and the items it says are not repaired, from zenodo/MANIFEST.json (its open defects and its entry for this concept), and from the files each line names, as they stand at the tag. The last two sections describe this deposit: what it holds, and each file's size, sha256 and md5, computed from the deposited bytes, with the source bundle's file count taken from the tag's tree.

Security: a capsule or an audited certificate chose where styxx wrote files (GHSA-h5xv-4344-f62r)

  • What was wrong. A v0.1 OATH capsule (styxx-oath/capsule/v0.1) embeds its document and its receipts as bytes, each under a name. python -m styxx.capsule verify FILE re-ran the certifier by writing those bytes to Path(tempdir) / name, and the capsule supplied the name. A path joined to an absolute name is that absolute name, and .. climbs out, so an absolute name or a ../ name was written outside the temporary directory: verifying a capsule someone else made could create or overwrite any file the user running the verifier can write, with bytes the capsule's author chose. The hash checks did not stop it, because the capsule also carries the certificate those bytes are checked against. styxx.charon's re-run of a v0.1 capsule (in ingest, verify and derive) wrote the same way. So did python -m styxx.corpus_audit with history on (the default for a full clone): it wrote a certificate's receipt bytes at the issuing commit under the receipt names the audited certificate gives, so auditing a repository someone else wrote could write outside its temporary directory.
  • Affected releases. 7.47.0 and 7.48.0, through python -m styxx.capsule verify (styxx.capsule.verify_capsule), which has been in the package since 2026-08-31; and 7.48.0, through styxx.charon and styxx.corpus_audit. Creating a capsule is not affected: it writes under the names of the files you hand it.
  • The repair (commits 76e9dcc5 and d8b856a1). Every embedded name must be a bare file name under POSIX and Windows rules alike: no separator, no drive, not . or .., no control character, no trailing dot or space, and no Windows device name. No two names may be the same file on a case-insensitive file system. Otherwise verify reports the name as a problem, writes nothing and does not re-run the certifier, so the capsule fails; charon records live_error: unsafe_embedded_name and writes nothing; corpus_audit writes nothing, re-derives nothing for that certificate and says why in its stands_reason. The ten v0.1 capsules committed under papers/ carry only names the rule accepts, and all ten still verify.
  • What to do. Upgrade: pip install -U styxx==7.48.1. Until you can, verify only capsules from a source you trust, or verify them in a throwaway environment (a container, a virtual machine or a disposable account) where a file written anywhere does no harm. The same holds for running python -m styxx.charon over capsules you did not make, and python -m styxx.corpus_audit over a repository you did not write (or run it with --history off).
  • The tests. tests/test_capsule_bare_names.py refuses an absolute receipt name, a ../ receipt name and a ../ document name with nothing written; holds charon to writing nothing where a forged capsule points; refuses two names that differ only in case; and pins the rule on 7 names it accepts and 19 it refuses. Run against 43b3b608, the commit this release branched from, the four tests of a name that escapes fail, the 26 cases that pin the rule fail because the rule is not there, and the honest-capsule and case-collision tests pass (on Windows). tests/test_corpus_audit_bare_names.py audits a throwaway repository whose certificate names a receipt ../../ out of the temporary directory, and one with an absolute name: nothing is written outside it. Run against 76e9dcc5 the climbing case fails; the absolute case passes there too, because that name never resolves to bytes at the issuing commit.
  • What it does not say. That the certifier is safe to run over arbitrary bytes. Verifying a capsule still re-runs the installed certifier over the embedded document and receipts; that is the design. This repair bounds where those bytes are written.

Also in this release

  • In the package since 7.48.0: python -m styxx.islands gains --island-z, and --demo reads its list at island_z=3 and prints the rule it used (#93); the library default stays 1.0. The PyPI description gives each AUC to the instrument that earned it.
  • In the repository, not the wheel: the #125 repair of the blind-packet builder, which now numbers items by their shuffled position (the committed EXTERNAL-1 packet keeps its leak; see below); the errata to [7.48.0] and the corrections on main from the audit of the 7.48.0 week's public text on 2026-09-29; 7.48.0's Zenodo record, with its receipts and the metadata as published and as corrected; the sworn action's docs (#164); and two tests that failed on Windows for reasons outside the code under test (#185, #186).
  • SECURITY.md said releases reach PyPI through Trusted Publishing with PEP 740 attestations. They do not: publish.yml uploads with an API token held as a repository secret and sets attestations: false. The file now says so, and its steps for checking a release compare SHA-256 sums only. The sums of the wheel and the sdist are listed below.
  • Cutting this release: styxx/_version.py is 7.48.1 (e2b31742), and CITATION.cff gives version 7.48.1 and date-released 2026-10-06 (3fc2c852). conformance/sworn/ was regenerated for the version stamp (e2b31742): 15 vectors took new ids, 0 moved, and no expected outcome changed; still 3620 vectors, 20 families and 3981 blobs. That CI passes on the regenerated set was not observed at the cut. README.md, which becomes the PyPI page, was audited at this cut against the tree it ships with: one line changed (2770cd70), and its tag-pinned links still point at the v7.48.0 tag.

Known stale or wrong lines in the deposited tree

  • The wheel and the tree still carry the priority claims and charter words that the errata to [7.48.0] list, in the docstrings of styxx/__init__.py, forecast.py, intercept.py, critique.py and hallucination.py, in attack/universal_suffixes_v0.json, adapters/guardrails.py and admissibility.py, and on README line 422. None of those files changed in this release, and that README line did not either.
  • README.md labels 10.5281/zenodo.19326174, the concept record of the Fathom research-paper series, as the always-latest DOI in its badge row and link table (open defects D3 and D4 in zenodo/MANIFEST.json). Its citation row names the software concept DOI, 10.5281/zenodo.19758618.
  • CITATION.cff names the software concept DOI, but GitHub's "Cite this repository" prompt renders its preferred-citation, the position paper 10.5281/zenodo.19777921, which predates that paper's 2026-06-21 scope erratum (D2 in zenodo/MANIFEST.json). Whether the prompt should cite the software is left to the maintainer.
  • web/gate/README.md's drift section and web/gate/differential/py_side.py still say 7.48.0 has not shipped.
  • The #125 repair makes the blind-packet builder, papers/closed-model-frontier/external1_packet.py, number items by their shuffled position by default. Its build --as-published mode reproduces the pre-repair bytes on purpose, leak included, because the committed EXTERNAL-1 packet, key and digest are receipts; that mode has been shown only on a synthetic ledger and shelf, not run on the real ones. The committed packet still carries the id leak, and whether any adjudicator used it cannot be re-tested.
  • zenodo/MANIFEST.json names 7.48.0 (10.5281/zenodo.23042251) as the latest version of this concept; this record supersedes that line.

Not in this deposit

This record holds the tagged tree and the two files PyPI serves for 7.48.1, and nothing else. Work merged to the default branch after the tag is not in it.

Files in this record

  • styxx-v7.48.1-source-bundle.zip: the source tree at tag v7.48.1: git archive --format=zip --prefix=styxx-7.48.1/ v7.48.1 run with core.autocrlf=false, so each of its 6043 files is byte-identical to its git blob (checked by blob id); the zip comment carries the commit id. 275578927 bytes; sha256 d50a7933fb668285fb21dfc34d2671cd2483b7d97e2068c2f4a20b07e140103c; md5 438ed1bd56ffb8cda4e95c82ec7fe20c
  • styxx-7.48.1-py3-none-any.whl: the wheel, as published on PyPI (sha256 checked against PyPI). 8043925 bytes; sha256 a5d8a6b3ba1e0070cda1cb69c5452cd68f22f8ecec286af7157594b5a47b9a31; md5 52cf80c432493b64ddff70cf9f513cb5
  • styxx-7.48.1.tar.gz: the sdist, as published on PyPI (sha256 checked against PyPI). 8593254 bytes; sha256 fde727642f4e6140c69d8c6805c810d26b5f6159deb7065c629999f74bce3da6; md5 e418930c1defb173dffbf37ba077db6a

Each file in the wheel outside its .dist-info directory, and each file in the sdist other than the build metadata its build generates (PKG-INFO, setup.cfg and styxx.egg-info/), is byte-identical to the tag's blob at the same path.

Reproduce the source bundle's contents from a clone: git -c core.autocrlf=false archive --format=zip --prefix=styxx-7.48.1/ v7.48.1. Every file it holds then equals its git blob; the zip's own sha256 can differ with the git and zlib versions that write it. Without core.autocrlf=false on a machine that sets it, git converts text files to CRLF inside the archive and the file contents differ.
